subject: ela
intro: Pick the complete sentence or right formality.

items.prompt:
Which is a COMPLETE sentence?
A) Ran fast
B) The dog ran fast
C) Fast and far

steps: Subject + verb + full thought. Key is B.

items.prompt:
A complete sentence needs a subject and a:
A) verb
B) color
C) number

Which is MORE formal?
A) Yeah, it's cool.
B) Yes, it is interesting.

steps: Complete and polite. Key is B.

items.prompt:
Why is 'Went to the park' NOT complete?
A) It has no verb
B) It is missing a subject (who went?)
C) It is too long
items.answer: B) It is missing a subject (who went?)

solution.answer: B) It is missing a subject (who went?)

items.prompt:
For a class presentation (formal), you should use:
A) complete, polite sentences
B) slang like 'gonna'
C) one-word answers

Which is a COMPLETE sentence?
A) We won the game.
B) Won the game.
C) The big game.

steps: Has subject and verb. Key is A.

items.prompt:
Which group of words is a complete sentence?
A) Because the rain stopped
B) The children played outside after the rain stopped.
C) After the rain
items.answer: B) The children played outside after the rain stopped.

steps: Full thought with subject and verb. Key is B.
solution.answer: B) The children played outside after the rain stopped.

items.prompt:
You are speaking to the whole school at an assembly. The BEST choice is to:
A) use complete sentences and formal, polite language
B) use slang and sentence fragments
C) mumble short phrases
items.answer: A) use complete sentences and formal, polite language

solution.answer: A) use complete sentences and formal, polite language
